correctness.rationale: For the Fibonacci recurrence matrix Q, the off-diagonal entry is F_n, its trace is L_n, and the off-diagonal entry of (Q^n)^2 is their product. The congruences Q^6=I mod 4 and Q^24=I mod 9 certify complete periods without requiring minimality. Independent recurrence calculation reproduced all 6 and 24 obstruction residues: modulo 4 the entries are 2 exactly at indices 0 and 3 and 3 otherwise, while modulo 9 the table is nowhere zero and hits a multiple of 3 only at 5,13,21, where it equals 3. Hence T_n is nonzero, the displayed valuations of |T_n| are exact, and neither 4 nor 9 divides T_n at any positive n. Complete additivity of P_b, valid even for noncoprime factors, would force equality of the digit sum of F_{2n} with the sum of the other two digit sums if all three were Smith. The digit congruence modulo b-1 would force b-1 to divide T_n. Either 4 or 9 dividing b-1 contradicts the complete-period certificates. The definition excludes noncomposites, including 1, so those indices do not pose exceptional Smith cases. Independent decimal-string recurrence and multiplication confirmed both transcribed factor products, F_827 L_827=F_1654, digit sums 809,802,1592, transcribed factors' sums 809 and 802, and deficit -19.
replay_paths: Compute Q powers modulo 4 and 9 by repeated matrix multiplication; alternatively advance (F_n,F_{n+1},L_n,L_{n+1}) by the recurrence from (0,1,2,1) until both pairs return after 6 or 24 steps. Tabulate F_n L_n-F_n-L_n along those proved periods.

For the example, advance separate F and L decimal arrays with exact addition, multiply the factor lists in frozen artifacts/verify.py by digit convolution with carry, and compare to the separately evolved F_827 and L_827. Continue F to 1654 and sum decimal digits. This independently yielded matching products and the displayed sums; no primality test was used.
residual_risks: Primality of the transcribed large factors is imported from the published Smith example and its factor sources, not independently certified. The all-index theorem is independent of this illustration and of any prime factorization.

value.rationale: The product F_n L_n is naturally singled out by the existing even-index Smith search and its known common Smith index, not by choosing an arbitrary recurrence or sampling modulus. The exact low-prime valuations resolve a factorization-free obstruction at all indices, explaining why the common-index phenomenon cannot persist under doubling as a triple, in decimal and uniformly for two base families. That complete restriction is useful in interpreting or extending expensive Smith searches. It is stronger than testing the known example and is not a claim about the rarity or uniqueness of the underlying pair.
residual_risks: The theorem does not rule out further common Smith indices for just F_n and L_n, and does not assert triple exclusion in every base.
